summary: Started out believing 1/3 and 1/4 are the same because each is one slice, then corrected it and explained why more slices means smaller slices. Has not yet tried a new pair of fractions alone.

objectives.label: The bottom number tells how many equal pieces the whole is cut into
objectives.note: The learner never said what the bottom number means.

objectives.label: A fair comparison needs wholes of the same size and equal pieces
objectives.quote: Same size pizzas, so more slices means each slice is smaller.
objectives.note: Used the same-size pizzas as the reason, without being told to.

objectives.label: More pieces of the same whole means smaller pieces, so 1/4 is smaller than 1/3
objectives.quote: Same size pizzas, so more slices means each slice is smaller.
objectives.note: First said the slices were the same. After seeing one on top of the other, gave the reason in their own words.

misconceptions.label: Thinks 1/3 and 1/4 are equal because both have one piece
misconceptions.quote: It doesn't matter. You both get one slice, so it's the same.
misconceptions.how_detected: Said it aloud, then circled one slice in each pizza

next_steps: Ask them to compare 1/6 and 1/8 with their own drawing and no help.
Ask what the bottom number of a fraction means; they have not put that into words yet.
